newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stainless trade warns of nickel surcharges.
newsitem.headline: German stainless trade warns of nickel surcharges.

text.p: High nickel prices are likely to bring rising surcharges in the German stainless steel sector, the trade and stockholders association Edelstahl handels vereinigung (EHV) said.
EHV also cited firm ferrochrome and molybdenum prices.
"A slight increase in March should be followed by another, more sizeable, surcharge in April," it said in a circular.
"Stockholders should consider these developments when planning future business decisions."
An EHV spokesman said surcharges in 18-10 percent chrome-nickel steel, with a 50-60 percent share in stainless output and trade, would rise to 340 marks a tonne in March from 310 marks in February.
The surcharge would rise to 460 marks in April.
This came in the context of recovering consumer demand for stainless steel products, EHV said.

Stocks of stainless sheet, for example, had been wound down over the last 18 months. Lead times at European stainless mills were lenghtening and producers were planning to raise ex-mill prices in the second quarter of 1997.
Stainless steel accounts for two-thirds of nickel use. Germany consumed an estimated 72,000-75,000 tonnes of nickel last year.
EHV left unchanged a November forecast that German stainless steel production might raise by three to five percent in 1997.
Output of stainless steel ingot, the raw material for finished flat and long products, was estimated at 1.35 million tonnes in 1996.
